jules: FYI saw a regression in staging this morning after the kernel selection change we rolled Friday. KV cache memory climbs steadily on long chat sessions and we hit OOM in a few runs. Starts ~6GB -> ~14GB over ~9m (same workload).

sophia: Yikes. Is this specific to INT8 quant path, or also BF16/FP16?

jules: Looks tied to mixed-precision rollout. Repro shows INT8 active pages + BF16 fallback on some layers. When fallback happens, slot metadata gets rewritten and the slot reference counts look off, which prevents reuse and causes page fragmentation.

runtime-bot: Profiling summary attached (pv: kv:slot_rewrites=3121, page_fragments=78, evict_ops=620, avg_lookup_latency=1.9ms, kernel_variant=kv-kernel-v2-quantopt).

maya: Can you paste the `kv_stats` from the repro? Also, which kernel selection rule triggered v2?

jules: Paste below (repro run, 3 warmups, then longctx 8k tokens):

```
KV_STATS {
  total_slots: 524288
  live_slots: 412734
  fragmented_pages: 78
  page_use_rate: 0.42
  eviction_count: 620
  avg_slot_age_ms: 18400
  int8_pages: 1984
  bf16_pages: 3024
  slot_rewrites: 3121
}
WARMUP_LOG: kernel_select -> kv-kernel-v2-quantopt (seq_dist matches longctx pref)
```

alan: From the numbers it feels like reuse == low because slot_rewrites are happening during fallback, effectively turning hot prefixes into new slots repeatedly. That explains growth rather than stable hit-rate.

ops-bot: Heap snapshot links: s3://redwood-perf/staging/kv/mixed-prec/kern-v2/1968504321/heap-1.hprof

sophia: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel-v2 changes kv page layout (slot alignment) so compaction doesn't collapse mixed-precision fragments; 2) the fallback path allocates temporary bf16 pages and doesn't update the kv compaction index correctly. Either would increase fragmentation.

jules: I instrumented compaction hooks and saw compaction runs but they skip ranges where `slot.version != page.expected_version` — looks like version bumps on fallback prevent compaction because we treat them as concurrent mutations.

maya: Can you reproduce with a forced older kernel? If kernel-v1 doesn’t jitter slot.version on fallback, that’d be telling.

jules: Re-ran with kernel pin to kv-kernel-v1: memory stays ~6.2GB steady. No repeated slot_rewrites. So v2 behavior is implicated.

alan: Two remediations: revert kernel selection for quantopt until we fix version bump logic, or implement a safe compaction path that tolerates transient version diffs by comparing stable keys instead of versions.

sophia: Another short-term test: add aggressive compaction at warmup end (force compact on prefix ranges). If that keeps memory under control, we can ship a heuristic while devs patch v2.

jules: I prototyped a warmup compaction flag: `--kv-warmup-compact=true`. With it, memory plateaued ~7.1GB instead of growing. Slight CPU spike on warmup but runtime stable.

ops-bot: Telemetry for flagged runs: compaction_time_ms +4200 (median), 99th latency unchanged, cost CPU bump ~3%.

maya: Accuracy/regression concerns: we also ran eval prompt-suite after forcing compaction + INT8 and saw a tiny perplexity drift (~0.6%) on a few prompts where fallback had been observed. Need to confirm it's compaction interaction and not quantization noise.

sophia: Good call. We must measure QA against baseline BF16 and INT8 no-compaction. Create a small A/B job on staging with token-level diff logging for the eval set.

alan: Quick patch idea: when fallback increments slot.version, also write a compacting tombstone marker that compaction will treat as safe to reclaim in the next cycle. Safer than broad version relaxation.

jules: I'll open a PR with the tombstone marker plus the warmup compact flag. Will also add a targeted perf test: longctx streaming 10k tokens, mixed-precision schedule with ~30% fallback events.

maya: Assign me to perf test and I'll wire the telemetry to the dashboard (per-route kv memory, compaction runs, slot_rewrites).

jules: Thanks — tagging @sophia for validation tests and @alan for kernel rollback plan if we need quick mitigate.

sophia: I'll run the A/B evaluation and post results here, aiming for within 4h. If accuracy drift >1% we revert selection.

alan: I'll prepare a rollback policy doc and an automated toggle to prefer kv-kernel-v1 for quantopt in the selector.

jules: TL;DR: kernel-v2 quantopt path causes slot version churn on fallback -> fragmented pages -> eviction thrash & memory growth. Short-term: warmup compaction flag works as a mitigation. Mid-term: tombstone + fix compaction logic or rollback kernel selection.

runtime-bot: Incident created: PERF-1223 (priority P2) — links: https://tracker/redwood/PERF-1223

ops-bot: Postmortem checklist item added to PERF-1223: add unit for `slot.version` semantics across fallback, extend compaction tests to mixed-precision flows.

jules: I'll open the PR and ping here when ready. :thumbsup:

sophia: thanks, team.
